messages:
alex_m: heads up — hit a regression after turning on activation checkpointing for the 8xA100 PP2/TP4 training-style workload. baseline p99 step ~120ms, with checkpointing it jumped to 240–280ms. looks like all-reduce times spiked and we lost comm/compute overlap. attaching the short perf dump below.

maya_r: ouch. is the kv cache involved? last time recompute caused cache churn for attention keys.

alex_m: yep suspected that. perf snippet (nvprof-style):

```
Host to Device memcpy: 0.5ms
Kernel forward_attn: 12.4ms
Kernel recompute_attn: 11.9ms
AllReduce (allreduce_fused): 0.7ms => 2.1ms (checkpoint on)
AllReduce (allreduce_fused): 0.6ms => 1.9ms (baseline)
AllReduce wait (peak): 18.2ms (checkpoint) vs 5.9ms (no checkpoint)
KV cache send: spike at backward pass +9.8ms
Total step: 125ms -> 268ms
```

jonah: can you paste the exact runtime flags and model config you ran? microbatch size, seq len, kv-cache mode, kernel-routing?

alex_m: run command: `./serve --model=redwood-alpha --pp=2 --tp=4 --microbatch=4 --seq=2048 --enable-activation-checkpointing=true --kv-cache=on --kernel-routing=auto`

sophia_ml: quick summary from the trace: when checkpointing is on we recompute saved activations during backward. if remat regions cross PP boundaries, each PP stage recompute triggers extra cross-stage sends for KV/cache and intermediate activations, which prevents overlap and amplifies all-reduce queuing. plus the recompute code path seems to select a different kernel variant that doesn't use the fused-reduce path. that explains the all-reduce time jump.

maya_r: aha. so two orthogonal causes: (1) cross-boundary recompute increases inter-stage comm; (2) kernel selection fallback kills fused all-reduce optimizations.

jonah: i ran a tiny repro: 2 layers, pp=2, checkpoint slicing: full-layer remat vs per-stage remat. results:
- per-layer remat aligned with PP stage: p99 ~130ms
- remat crossing stage boundary: p99 ~240ms

jonah: enabling `enable_recompute_kernel_opt=true` reduces all-reduce latency by ~40% in the crossing case (so kernel-routing fix is promising).

alex_m: suggestion: default policy should avoid placing remat boundaries across pipeline stage boundaries unless user explicitly requests cross-boundary remat. also we should prefer recompute kernels that maintain fused-allreduce semantics.

sophia_ml: agreed. other mitigations: increase microbatching to expose more compute for overlap, add a quick path to skip KV re-send on recompute when keys unchanged (we already have a checksum for KV entries), and add a tiny caching layer per-PP-stage to hold recomputed KV until next step.

maya_r: small note: bumped batch size helped overlap but also increased memory pressure. for a few customers microbatch increase is acceptable but not a universal fix.

alex_m: open questions for infra team: can we change kernel selection heuristics without risking regression on other archs? and do we have perf tests that would have caught this?

infra-bot: perf-ci queued: job id 45213, compare baseline vs checkpoint-branch.

jonah: actionables i can pick up: (1) microbenchmark toggling `enable_recompute_kernel_opt` across A100/H100, (2) add unit test that asserts no remat region spans PP boundaries by default and warns if it does, (3) dataset in perf-ci that runs pp/tp/recompute permutations.

sophia_ml: i'll draft a short RFC: remat alignment policy + recompute kernel contract (must preserve fused allreduce or expose opt-in fallback). include a small warning in console when users enable cross-boundary remat.

alex_m: i'll open the perf PR with traces, nvprof snippets, and a proposed kernel-routing patch (experimental flag first). tagging @maya_r and @jonah for review — can we pair tomorrow? :calendar:

maya_r: yep, i'll help validate on H100 too. also will try the KV checksum skip for recompute.

jonah: will add the perf regression test to perf-ci and run across the supported Docker images.

alex_m: thanks. logging this thread reference for follow-up. if anyone hits similar symptoms, paste the short nvprof snippet and the `--kernel-routing` value.

sophia_ml: nice find — this explains the noisy all-reduce spikes we've seen in a few customer reports. good path forward. :+1:
